title: Adaptive contract signaller for usage ingest
creator: Maya R. Chen
description:
Problem: The console usage pipeline sees a growing tail of mildly malformed or out-of-contract events that bypass rigid validation and later cause downstream analytics failures, elevated SLO errors, and hard-to-debug dedupe/normalization mismatches. Current gateway validators either accept too much (resulting in noisy downstream consumers) or reject too aggressively (leading to customer telemetry loss).

Goal: Build a lightweight runtime component — the Adaptive Contract Signaller (ACS) — that runs at ingest time to classify events into: exact-match, hint-match, soft-deviation, and unknown. ACS will emit rich signals and apply a conservative safety throttle for unknown or high-risk shapes while allowing graceful acceptance of hint-match events. The signals will drive routing, staged schema upgrades, backpressure, and targeted replays for repair.

Scope: implement ACS as a horizontally-scalable, low-latency gRPC service colocated with the existing ingest gateway; provide a registry of contract fingerprints; expose metrics and traces; surface a control plane endpoint for adjusting thresholds and rollout policies. The work includes API compatibility, integration tests with the ingest gateway, Datadog dashboards, and a canary rollout plan.
tasks: Design ACS API and proto (gRPC) + contract fingerprint format
Implement fast fingerprint matcher with LRU cache (Go) and optional Bloom prefilter
Integrate ACS as a synchronous call in ingest-gateway with a 5ms tail latency budget
Emit signals to event-router (topic: ingest.contract-signals) and update routing rules to respect signals
Add safety throttle that can apply token-based backpressure and a degradable acceptance mode
Create integration tests simulating contrived contract drift and high-throughput load
Build Datadog dashboards and SLO alerts: signalled_rate, unknown_shape_rate, throttle_applied_count, extra_latency_p50/p95
Prepare migration/runbook and canary rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with automatic rollback criteria
acceptance_criteria: ACS responds within 5ms p95 for 95% of requests at baseline traffic
Unknown_shape_rate decreases downstream consumer exceptions by >= 60% in canary
Backpressure triggers when unknown_shape_rate > 0.5% for sustained 1 minute, and rollout obeys automatic rollback rules
Integration tests and end-to-end pipeline run succeed in staging with synthetic contract drift
Datadog dashboards and runbook documented and reviewed by SRE
Feature flag controlled; ability to opt-out customers and pin to previous validator behavior
technical_notes: Use 64-bit Murmur3 fingerprint over stable canonicalized event shape (field names + types + presence) to avoid storing full schemas
Implement 'semantic hints' table: lightweight heuristics (enum cardinality, time-windowed field-appearance) to classify hint-match vs soft-deviation
Provide configurable policies: throttle_threshold, hint_accept_window, fallback_policy (accept/reject/throttle) per-customer and per-route
Persist fingerprint registry in a small strongly-consistent store (initially Postgres with changefeed to a Redis cache) with a compact on-disk snapshot for fast warmup
Expose GRPC health and readiness; use request tracing headers to carry decision id for downstream correlation
